item.title: IASTM for Hamstring Region
clinicalUse: Adjunct for chronic hamstring-related stiffness/pain after acute injury phase
contact: Instrument over muscle belly, avoiding ischial region if highly irritable and avoiding sciatic nerve pathway pressure.
dosage: 30–90 seconds per area, few minutes total.
item.visualCue: Tool along hamstring muscle belly → short dose → active load re-test.

subTechniques.name: Gluteal muscles — IASTM
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, prone or side-lying with pelvis stabilized.
subTechniques.contact: Appropriate instrument edge over intact skin at Gluteal muscles with conservative pressure.
subTechniques.direction: Use light-to-moderate scanning/treatment strokes; bruising is not the goal.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 30–120 seconds per small area followed by active movement/loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
